editorial:
Imagine moving your whole family to a tiny, quiet village in Norway to escape a tragedy. That is exactly what Mihai and Lisbet do after losing their parents. You will feel the hope they have as they try to start over and make friends with their kind neighbors, the Halbergs. At first, everything feels peaceful and cozy, but that feeling disappears quickly. The mood shifts the moment their daughter, Elia, comes home from school with bruises on her skin. It turns the story from a quiet family drama into a tense mystery that makes you question who you can actually trust.

The acting is top-notch and makes the family's pain feel real. While the story starts slow, the tension builds up in a way that keeps you glued to your seat. You might find some parts a bit sad, but the payoff is worth it. If you have a high-end TV, you should definitely stream this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see the beautiful Norwegian scenery. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you find out that the Halbergs were not as kind as they seemed. The bruises on Elia were caused by the Halberg son during a secret bullying spree. The movie ends with a huge confrontation where the families face the truth. Instead of a happy ending, the Gheorghius decide to leave the village for good, realizing that some places are too broken to ever truly call home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gripping family mysteries and emotional stories.
